lines.narration: In this town, everyone wears a price tag. Whoever pays it, owns you.
The Mayor cost nine million. The sheriff, four. I cost one dollar.
People used me as a tip jar.
Then a gray-coat stranger arrived, and started buying everyone.
The butcher. The sheriff. The choir. Sold. Sold. Sold.
He skipped me. 'Not you. You're not for sale, you're the deposit.'
By midnight, the whole town marched behind him, gray-eyed.
At dawn, he handed me one dollar. Exact change.
I held it. The empty town held its breath.
'Full refund,' he said. 'The buyer backed out.'
Then every tag in town flipped to the same number. One dollar.
The tags were never prices. They were installments.
Everyone in this town has a price. I'm the price.
Tonight, I was finally paid off.
